# Load Data

```{r}
# Load dataset
games <- read.csv("../../../data/games.csv")

# Basic characteristics
str(games)
cat("Missing values:" , sum(is.na(games)))
```

# Task 2

## Collecting Ideas

When reading the assignment I have 2 main ideas:

- Idea 1: we assume that different time controls represent different game modes, therefore different distributions in rating. My first idea would be to model a hierarchical model capturing the different populations of games assuming a general underlying player strength.

- Idea 2: Besides the general underlying player strength players could have strength in different game modes eg., R1 \> R2 for one game mode but R1 \< R2 in a different game mode.

## Continue with Idea 2

By further reading, I think Idea 2 is expected one. Therefore I will continue with that one as we by the note we assume linear dependence of timecontrol, ie.:

$$\boxed{R_j(t_c)=\alpha_j+\beta_j x(t_c)}$$

where $x(t_c)$ is the z-scaled game duration.

- $\alpha_j$: Base strength of engine $j$, modeled in exactly the same way as \(R_j\) in Task 1 (with draws).
- $\beta_j$: How its strength changes with thinking time, with $$\beta_j\sim\mathcal N(0,100^2).$$
- $t_c=\text{time}+40\cdot\text{increment}$: time as a numeric variable.

### Data Preparation for Stan

```{r}
# Engine identifiers
engines <- sort(unique(c(games$white, games$black)))

# Convert time controls into expected game duration
parts <- strsplit(games$timecontrol, "\\+")

tc <- vapply(parts, function(p) {
  as.numeric(p[1]) + 40 * as.numeric(p[2])
}, numeric(1))

# Standardize time control
tc_center <- mean(tc)
tc_scale <- sd(tc)
stopifnot(is.finite(tc_scale), tc_scale > 0)

x <- (tc - tc_center) / tc_scale

# Encode the three game outcomes
outcome_levels <- c("1-0", "1/2-1/2", "0-1")

# Data for the time-control model
stan_data_tc <- list(
  N = nrow(games),
  K = length(engines),
  white = match(games$white, engines),
  black = match(games$black, engines),
  outcome = match(games$result, outcome_levels),
  x = as.numeric(x)
)
```

### Posterior Sampling

```{r, results='hide'}
# Compile time-control model
mod_tc <- cmdstan_model("helpers/rating_timecontrol.stan")

# Sample from the posterior
fit_tc <- mod_tc$sample(
  data = stan_data_tc,
  seed = 42
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Parameter estimates and MCMC diagnostics
summary_tc <- fit_tc$summary(
  variables = c("intercept", "slope", "draw_tendency")
)

knitr::kable(
  summary_tc[, c(
    "variable", "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Time-Control Model: Posterior Summary and Diagnostics"
)
```

The MCMC diagnostics indicate satisfactory sampling performance. All R-hat values are close to 1, all bulk effective sample sizes exceed 1,000 and all tail effective sample sizes exceed 100. Thus, the sampling diagnostics do not indicate convergence problems.

# Results

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Extract estimated baseline ratings
base_ranking <- fit_tc$summary(variables = "intercept")

base_ranking$Engine <- engines

base_ranking <- base_ranking[
  order(-base_ranking$mean),
  c("Engine", "mean", "sd")
]

knitr::kable(
  base_ranking,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Engine Ranking at Average Time Control"
)
```

The estimated ratings at the average time control are very similar to those obtained in Task 1, yielding the same ranking: E > A > SM > C > B > D. Posterior standard deviations are also comparable. However, the time-dependent model additionally allows relative engine strengths to change across different time controls.

```{r}
# Extract posterior samples for base ratings and time effects
alpha <- as.matrix(fit_tc$draws(
  variables = "intercept", format = "draws_matrix"
))

beta <- as.matrix(fit_tc$draws(
  variables = "slope", format = "draws_matrix"
))

# Calculate engine ratings at a given time control
rating_at_time <- function(t) {
  x <- (t - tc_center) / tc_scale
  alpha + beta * x
}
```

We visualize the posterior mean ratings across different time controls to examine how engine strength changes with game duration.

```{r}
# Define time controls from 15 to 600 seconds
times <- seq(15, 600, length.out = 100)

# Calculate expected ratings for each engine and time control
ratings <- t(sapply(times, function(t) {
  colMeans(rating_at_time(t))
}))

# Plot time-dependent ratings for all engines
matplot(times, ratings, type = "l", lty = 1,
        xlab = "Time Control (seconds)",
        ylab = "Expected Rating")

legend("topright", legend = engines,
       col = 1:6, lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

The plot shows that Engine E remains the strongest, while the other engines exhibit different time-dependent trends, motivating separate tier lists for the four specified time controls.

```{r}
# Rank engines based on their ratings at a given time control
tier_ranking <- function(t) {
  draws <- rating_at_time(t)
  means <- colMeans(draws)
  idx <- order(-means)

  # Calculate superiority probabilities between neighboring engines
  p <- sapply(1:(length(engines) - 1), function(i) {
    mean(draws[, idx[i]] > draws[, idx[i + 1]])
  })

  # Assign a new tier if superiority probability exceeds 95%
  data.frame(
    Tier = c(1, 1 + cumsum(p >= 0.95)),
    Engine = engines[idx],
    Mean = means[idx],
    SD = apply(draws, 2, sd)[idx]
  )
}
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Generate tier lists for the four requested time controls
knitr::kable(tier_ranking(15), digits = 1, caption = "Tier List: 15+0")

knitr::kable(tier_ranking(60), digits = 1, caption = "Tier List: 60+0")

knitr::kable(tier_ranking(260), digits = 1, caption = "Tier List: 180+2")

knitr::kable(tier_ranking(600), digits = 1, caption = "Tier List: 600+0")
```

Engine E consistently occupies the highest tier, while the remaining rankings change with time control. Particularly at 600+0, increased posterior uncertainty prevents a clear separation of the other engines under our 95% superiority criterion.
